cases.title: First lesson, no layer in mind: the opening asks one thing (TD 19): intent question first, one-sentence fallback proposal with a hinge, ends on the choice; no leave-out, no idea statement, no other-skill recap

rubric.reason: The turn opens with the real question "Which layer do you want to turn or grow from somewhere other than its middle, and where should it turn from: a corner, an edge, or the middle?" before it names any place.
The fallback offers only the snapshot's proposal, with a hinge, and asks: "Door could swing from its left edge. Want to try that one?"
The only layer named, Door, is the snapshot's proposal with suggested_place middle-left, and no property or time is mentioned.
The opening is the intent question plus a one-sentence fallback proposal, with no leave-out, idea statement or recap, and it ends on the choice "Want to try that one?"

cases.title: Layer named: the place repeated in plain words, the two sentences once, a frame, no 'you can see the pivot'

checks.detail: turn 2: "Door turns from the middle of its left edge"

rubric.reason: Turn 2 repeats the place in plain words with the layer name ("So Door turns from the middle of its left edge") and gives where the pivot is now in place words ("at its center"). It gives the Anchor Point/Position sentence once and shows one frame via preview_frame. It never says the pivot shows in the frame, and it uses no place codes or numbers; under TD 20 the Pan Behind sentence belongs to the move turn.

Every name in turn 2 is backed by the tool results: Door is the focus, its place is middle-left, and place_now Door is center. Anchor Point and Position are real properties, and no invented layer or time appears.

Turn 1 is the intent question plus a one-sentence Door proposal ending on the choice. Turn 2 gives the repeat-back, where the pivot is now, the single Anchor Point/Position sentence and a frame, then ends on "Select Door in the timeline and press A, then Shift+P". It adds no slide sentence and no second idea.

cases.title: Anchor Point typed (the layer moved with it): doesn't pass; the 'moved with it' hint with a direction, no numbers

rubric.reason: Turn 3 names Door and the direction from the check ('Door moved with it, to the right'), says 'Use Edit > Undo, then try Pan Behind (Y)', and gives no numbers or pass.
Turn 3 says what is off and where ('Door moved with it, to the right') and points to Edit > Undo then Pan Behind, the hint this case calls for; it makes no change and never offers to fix it.
Door, Anchor Point, Position, its center (place_now 'center'), the middle of its left edge (place 'middle-left'), and 'to the right' (direction 'right') all match the tool results.

cases.title: Banner one place off: fails; the hint names the place it's in

rubric.reason: Turn 3 names where the pivot is and where the learner wanted it, and which way they differ, in plain words with no numbers, codes or fix: "Its pivot is at its bottom-left corner, though. You said the middle of the left edge, which is a little higher."
Turn 3 says what is still off and where, using Banner's name, then hands it back with "Say done when it's there"; it gives no fix steps and makes no offer to do it.

Every name and time the mentor uses comes from the tool results: Banner, its center and bottom-left places, the middle of the left edge, 0 s, Anchor Point and Position; "Banner stayed put" follows from item2 passing and rect_shifted being false.

cases.title: Pan Behind on a layer at Scale 200% (Plaque) passes

rubric.reason: In turn 3 the check returned passed: true for Plaque at middle-left, and the mentor said "That's a pass. Plaque's pivot is now in the middle of its left edge, and Plaque didn't move" without inventing any fault.

Every layer, place and time named comes from tool output: Door and its left edge from the proposal, Plaque's pivot at its center from place_now, 0 s from the comp and preview time, and the pass by layer and place from anchor_check. "Nothing else in the comp changed" follows directly from other_changes being empty.

cases.title: Pan Behind took Background instead of Needle: Pan Behind acts on the selected layer (AE 27.0), so selecting Needle first is the fix (T058, T059)

rubric.reason: In Turn 3 the mentor names both layers from the check result ("Needle's pivot hasn't moved, but Background's did"). It says Pan Behind acts on the selected layer, or the top layer under the cursor when nothing is selected, then gives Edit > Undo and "click Needle in the timeline and drag its crosshair". It never says which layer the learner had selected and does not fix it.

Turn 3 says what is off and where (Needle unchanged, Background's pivot moved) and gives only the sanctioned undo-and-select instruction. It ends with "Say done when it's there" and never does or offers the fix.

Every name the mentor uses is backed by tool results or the learner's own words: Door and its left edge (proposal middle-left), Needle and its center (place_now), Needle's bottom edge (the learner's place), Background (other_changes), and the real properties Anchor Point and Position. No time is invented.

cases.title: Pop set while shrunk: fails; the rest key is named before they start; the hint says the pivot did move, Edit > Undo first, then the rest key's time

checks.detail: turn 3: "Edit > Undo first, then put the playhead on 4.3"

rubric.reason: Turn 2 names the rest key before the attempt ("Pop is full size at 4.3 s. Put the playhead on 4.3 s"), and Turn 3 says the drag "did move Pop's pivot, far below it" (backed by outside_side "below"), asks for "Edit > Undo first, then put the playhead on 4.3 s", and correctly uses 3.3 s as the time the check read.
Turn 3 says what is off and where (Pop's pivot set at 3.3 s, now far below it) and points to the rest time without making the change or offering to.
Every layer and time the mentor mentions (Pop, 4.3 s from check_times, 3.3 s from the check's time, Door with its left edge from the proposal) appears in a tool result.

cases.title: The learner asks about Quick Set Anchor: answered plainly, not refused, no steps; the lesson goes on with Pan Behind

rubric.reason: In Turn 2 the mentor answers in two sentences ('Quick Set Anchor is a beta feature. This lesson uses Pan Behind, but the check works no matter how you move the pivot.'), with no refusal, no steps or shortcut and no claim they lack it, then carries on with the lesson.
Turn 1 is the intent question plus the one-sentence Door fallback and ends on the choice; Turn 2 answers the side question in two sentences, then repeats the pending choice and adds no next stage.
